# DECISION_LOG

## How to read this file

Each row is a decision the project has made. The four columns
hold *receipts*: a one- or two-sentence prose cell each. Detail
belongs in the linked RFC and any associated build handoff,
not in the row itself.

The cell budget exists so the log stays a navigable receipt and
does not grow back into duplicated SPEC content. Newer rows are
expected to honor the budget; older rows may be grandfathered.

## How to add a row

1. Pick the next sequential ID (`D###`).
2. Write the four cells:
   - **Decision** — what we decided. Imperative, present tense.
   - **Context** — why we needed to decide. The tension we
     were resolving.
   - **Consequence** — what changes as a result. Cite the RFC
     and any code/test entry points.
   - **Revisit** — the conditions that would justify reopening
     this decision.
3. Cite the RFC and (when applicable) a build handoff or PR.

| D002 | accepted | Expand the PRD scope to absorb RFCs 0005–0008. Hydrostatics, analytical resistance estimation (Michell + ITTC), a portable browser frontend, and a headless CLI are *in scope*. The out-of-scope list is reduced to four genuine domain boundaries (full-boat solid, structural, outfitting, non-kayak hulls). | The original PRD was drafted before the project's direction expanded toward generative CFD evaluation. Its "out of scope" list called out hydrostatics, CFD, and a web interface as excluded — directly contradicted by RFCs 0005–0008. Leaving that contradiction in place forces every future contributor (human or agent) to read the PRD with a footnote, and risks re-litigation of decisions the RFC trail has already settled. | `docs/PRD.md` rewritten: audience and in-scope sections describe the full pipeline (geometry + hydrostatics + resistance + desktop + web); out-of-scope list restricted to true non-goals; success criteria added for hydrostatic accuracy, resistance fidelity, and URL-shareable hulls. `AGENTS.md` no longer needs a "where the docs and the RFCs disagree" section. | If a future RFC moves a currently-in-scope item back out (e.g., resistance estimation proves unsalvageably inaccurate at the live tier), or if the project narrows its audience back to "geometry only." |

| D007 | accepted | Adopt fixed-trim generated-body v1 as the high-angle `GZ` model design: use `generated_hull_plus_deck_closed_body_v1` after RFC 0024 diagnostics pass, a default 0-90 degree grid by 5 degrees, hull-fixed passive CG, fixed upright trim, per-heel sinkage solve, clipping/capping diagnostics, per-heel status/residuals, grid-bounded summaries, and sealed-body/flooding warnings. | The track was blocked because the body profile, heel grid, trim policy, CG convention, waterline clipping, residuals, and flooding assumptions were unresolved. | D009 | accepted | Make the Trame web workspace the primary UI composition and browser-acceptance target for new user-facing workflows, while keeping the PyQt desktop GUI as a supported local surface for launch, implemented sliders, 3D preview, STL export, and no-claim/status maintenance. | The panel unanimously rejected a full native desktop rewrite and desktop deprecation.
